decisions: This is a deviation from the spec's wording, and the parent can override it. Sets are introduced when any set reaches level 1 or more, not strictly at "2 or more items of one set". Two distinct items of one set always reach level 1, because every item is worth at least 1 point and the threshold is 2. A single ★2 item also reaches level 1, and that bonus is live, so hiding it would hide a real stat change. The shop shows sets at that moment through a live check, and a 250 ms poll in ui.ts persists the flag through disclose().

Flags are stored as sys:<id> entries in settings.tutorialSeen, one per system ('sets' plus each ReactionId), plus a 'sys' marker for profiles tracked since disclosure exists. tutorial.ts used to hold its own copy of tutorialSeen and wrote it back on every step, and Replay and Skip replaced the list, so foreign ids were lost. The tutorial now reads the settings every tick. freshProgress(seen) and skipAll(seen) keep ids that are not tutorial steps or tips. This was the root cause to fix first, because without it 'introduced forever' would not hold.

Veteran migration: on first load, a profile without the 'sys' marker that has profile.stats.runs > 0 gets every system marked as met. Existing players keep seeing everything, which is how the spec's 'for new players' is implemented. Fresh profiles only get the marker, so they keep meeting systems after their first runs. A unit test with stubbed localStorage covers this.

The double-pack stickers ('2-pack', the '2×' mark and the inspector note) stay visible while sets are hidden. They explain the 1.5× price even though their text mentions set points. What is hidden: the receipt set panel, the offer-card set badges (setBadges), the inspector set chips, the set level-up card, and the run-history set icons.

The set explainer is a one-shot tutorial TIP 'sets' that reuses the bubble machinery. It is anchored at #shop .sets and placed above it, because the level-up card appears below the receipt at the same moment. Its trigger is a new Snap field setActive, which is persistent run state rather than a per-shop flag, so the tip is not lost if the first qualifying shop is busy with tutorial steps. Skip marks it seen like every other tip.

The reaction banner reuses the gold celebrate pop-up (the 'New combo!' card) with the title 'New reaction!', the reaction name and a one-line description. celebrate's icon is now optional. A 250 ms poll in ui.ts calls disclose(), and engine/reactions.ts gains only a desc key per entry in REACTION_TEXT. #banner was not used because wave and boss announcements also use it and would clobber each other. Lab, sim and bot runs never show it or record it.

No element called 'build stats' exists, so the 'what changed' line sits under the combos panel in the middle column. It is the last element there, so nothing shifts. It lists weapon damage and interval deltas matched by uid, combos formed or lost, and set level changes (only while sets are shown), computed from the before and after computeBuild results. Numbers are compared as displayed, so float noise never makes a line. The line also covers the Combine button, which is a merge. It clears after 4 s or at the next drop, and a drop that changes nothing removes it.

Active slots needed no code change. The HUD chips come from activeSlots(...).filter(a => a.slot), and the cart badges come from slotOfUid. Both cover only active items placed in the cart, so a profile without one sees no Q/E/F chips. The new test pins this (gridHtml badge plus HUD data) and passes on base by design. This is the one exception to 'each new test fails on base'.

★3 teaser: the new star3Teaser(id, tier) in i18n/data.ts renders ItemText.star3 with the ★3 numbers, strips the content's leading '★3: ' and wraps the rest in star3At ('At ★3: {line}' / 'Bei ★3: {line}'). It shows only below ★3. itemRules is untouched, so text.json does not change. Offer cards clamp the teaser to 2 lines with the full text in title, and the card art shrinks so it fits. The inspector shows it dimmed under the rules. tipMerge now mentions the ★3 bonus.

The 'Show all systems' setting is a checkbox (data-sys, special-cased in onInput before the generic data-set handler). Ticking it marks every system as met. It then renders as checked and disabled, because met systems stay met. A browser check confirmed the title settings modal stays open and the box becomes checked and disabled.

Tests outside the unit: set-points-ui.test.ts now calls showAllSystems() in beforeAll so its set-point assertions keep running for a profile that has met sets. The tutorial.test.ts snap factory gained setActive: false.

The veteran screenshots were set up in the page through dynamic module imports (showAllSystems, tutorialDone, profile runs) rather than the load-time migration. Sims run as lab runs and always show everything, so the fresh and veteran shots start a real run through the js arg (flow.startRun then devEndWave) instead.
open: Minor: players who were already veterans before this unit see the new set explainer tip once, the first time they have an active set. Adding the tip id 'sets' to the migration list in src/state/disclosure.ts would suppress it, at the cost of coupling disclosure to a tutorial id. Not done.

Minor: the reaction pop-up (top centre, 2.8 s) can briefly overlap a combat tutorial bubble when a fresh profile triggers a reaction during aisle 1. Two elements are needed for a reaction, so this is unlikely in practice.
Minor: on offer cards the ★3 teaser is clamped to 2 lines, so long lines end with an ellipsis. The full text is in the title tooltip and in the hover inspector.
Minor: during the first-shop tutorial, the 'combos' step bubble can sit over the change line, because it prefers the area below the combos panel.

nonBlocking: src/state/disclosure.ts: setActive uses 'any set level > 0', so a single ★2 item (2 tier-weighted points) also introduces sets. The spec says '2 or more items of one set'. This matches the tier-weighted points the base branch added, but it is a literal deviation worth a line in the report.

src/ui/tutorial-core.ts: the sets explainer is a TIP, not a step. A veteran whose tutorialSeen has no 'sets' id sees it once, and a profile that pressed Skip never sees it, because skipAll marks every tip seen. This is acceptable but not exactly 'when it first happens'.

tests/disclosure.test.ts: the active-slots test passes on the base branch (it only pins existing behavior, as the commit message says). The reaction test checks disclose() and the i18n strings, not the DOM banner that ui.ts shows through celebrate().

src/i18n/ui.ts: German chgSet reads 'Küche-Set Stufe 2 → 1' because tagT returns 'Küche'; 'Küchen-Set' would read better. The Settings label is 'Alle Systeme zeigen (Sets, Reaktionen)' with a suffix, where the spec names the toggle 'Show all systems'.

src/ui/shop.ts: the empty <div class="sets"> stays in the receipt while sets are hidden (margin-top: 10px). The change line is not cleared when the shop closes and reopens within 4 s. Both are cosmetic.
The reaction banner and the sets-introduced flag are written by a 250 ms setInterval in ui.ts rather than an event. It works and is guarded for null state, lab and bot runs.

decisions: Results, stock pool, Day, seed 1 (seed 2 in brackets). Each pair runs from integration 038fff7 to final. Win rate 48.8% (48.3%) to 28.3% (28.5%); target 20-35, met. Aisle 4 share of all deaths 39.7% to 23.3%; target under 28, met. Merges per run 2.94 to 2.73 (2.85); target at least 2.0, met. Combos at run end 2.60 to 2.41; target at least 2.0, met. ★3 items per run 0.28 to 0.22 (0.24); target at least 0.15, met. HP lost in aisle 2 0.23 to 1.11, and aisle 1 2.24 to 4.07. Starting pool win rate 60.5% to 39.0%; target at most 55, met. Evening 28.5% to 14.8%, or 15.7% on seeds 1 + 2 pooled; target at least 12 and near 15, met. Late 16.2% to 4.2%. Kitchen L3 at run end 53.7% to 18.5%, Tools L3 52.5% to 22.2%. All numbers are build-lab proxy numbers. The raw reports are in scratchpad/balance/ (m0-*, k5-*, tsv-*).

Step 1 findings note. The units pushed balance in one direction. The stock pool's openers and owned weight tripled merges, tier-weighted sets put Kitchen and Tools at L3 in more than half the runs, base interest raised the coins at every shop, and the ★3 behaviors went from 0.02 to 0.28 ★3 items per run. Win rate went from 26% (the old pool-all baseline, so a different pool) to 49%. Aisle 4 took 40% of all deaths because the aisles after it became easy.
Restock was skipped. Merges stayed between 2.65 and 2.94 at every step, above the 2.0 threshold, so the offer was not added.

Knobs applied in order: SET_THRESHOLDS 2/3/4 to 2/4/6. Aisles 1-2 shortened from 60 s to 38 s. Spitter and expired moved into aisle 3, turkey and cereal out of aisle 4. MINI_BOSS.hp 340 to 260 to 240. hpScale for aisles 5-7 from 1.7/2.0/2.3 to 1.8/2.2/2.6. dmgScale for aisles 5-7 from 1.6/1.7/1.8 to 1.7/1.85/2.0. Boss aisle hpScale 2.0 to 2.6 and dmgScale 1.7 to 2.1. Evening hpMult 1.2 to 1.1. Each commit message carries its before and after numbers. docs/balance-hillclimb.tsv rows 13-22 were measured by checking out each commit, and scratchpad/balance/tsvrows.sh reruns them.

Acceptance rule (my choice). One seed of 600 runs has a win-rate standard error of about 2 points. I accepted a knob when seeds 1 and 2, pooled to 1200 runs, moved past that noise. I also ran a paired sign test over the same seeds: for each run, did the win flip either way between before and after. The values were z -2.9 (hp), -4.3 (dmg), -6.1 (boss), 3.6 for the mini-boss's aisle-4 deaths at 240, and +2.5 for Evening.
I counted a group of per-aisle values in one table row as one knob. hpScale for aisles 5-7 is one commit, and so is dmgScale for aisles 5-7.

Vacuum ★3 (not dictated). The spec's example, a slow on each pulse, would copy Cold Storage, which already gives the pulse a slow. So from ★3 each damage pulse knocks back the groceries within 40 px of the cart's edge, with knockback 150 (about 50 px). The gate is hasStar3, and the numbers live in the tune (nozzle, blowback). pickupMult was removed. The tests cover ★2, ★3 and ★4. A real-game smoke shot of the weapon-vacuum sim showed no page errors. The lab does not model knockback, so it shows no win-rate effect.

EVENT_LEAD = 10 s (not dictated). rollEvent now caps the start window at the aisle's duration minus 10, so the wet floor (window up to 35 s) still matters in the 38 s aisle 2. The roll still uses the same two flow.rng draws.
Aisle 1-2 totals stayed at 30 and 33. The shorter duration alone raises enemies per second by about 70%. Side effect: aisle-1 leftovers rose from 2.5 to 8.8, and shop-1 coins fell from 28.1 to 25.5.

The codex order changed: CODEX_ENEMIES now lists expired before turkey and cereal, to match the new first aisles. I updated the pin enemyAppears('turkey').first from 4 to 5 on purpose, and added a test that aisle 4 brings no new grocery type.
Mini-boss HP became the aisle-4 lever. Most aisle-4 deaths came after its enrage. Cutting aisle-4 total or hpScale and delaying the enrage moved the share far less (logged in docs/buildlab.md).
The boss aisle's dmgScale also scales the Store Manager's own hits, not only the escorts'. Its death rate went from 16% to 27%.

I rejected higher counts for aisles 5-7 (58/62/68 measured -5 pts) because an earlier pass cut counts after a too-crowded complaint. I also rejected inflationPerShop 0.15, interestCap 2, WAVE_RAMP.hp 0.7, and the aisle-3 hp and count changes. All are logged in docs/buildlab.md.

Goal needs were recalibrated to 10-30% on the final Day stock state, seeds 1 + 2 pooled. pricegun: win with Checkout L1 (17.0%). leafblower: aisle 4+ (18.6%). doublebag: 4 combos (17.9%). goldstar: maxTier-1 against 2, so progress starts at 0 (18.5%). scoby: 500 (12.5%). barter: 380 (20.1%). binder: changed to win with a set at L3, because L3 is the cap and a run ending with an L3 set was 49% (21.7%). bowlingball: 10 (11.6%). snowcone: win with Frost L1 (14.0%). moldybread: 1, text 'Trigger a Detonate in one run' (10.4%; Detonate only occurs in about 10% of builds, so need 2 already falls below 10%). energy (24.3%) and laser (19.4%) are unchanged. goalBest is not on master, so no save migration is needed. The EN and DE texts were updated together.

Pins I updated on purpose. About 40 test files had carts that reached a set level with ★1 members or pinned that a lone ★3 is L2. They now use ★2 members, or say L1. The src/sims carts and notes (kitchen-heat, frost-cleaning, blast, electric-l3, dash-tools, snacks-defense, shred-tools-dash, weaken-cleaning, wet-*, affinity-*, weapon-*) were adjusted the same way, and a sim notes-vs-levels scan found none left wrong. No other tuning went through tests.

The golden set carts (tests/golden/carts.ts) now use ★2 for members 3 and 4, so set.<id>.L3 is still covered under 2/4/6. A new test checks each set cart's level. This change is also where the buffs.set.* leaves in text.json come from.

Checked and left alone: the Pressure Cooker ★3. A ★3 Cooker appeared in 1 of 70 runs that ended with a Cooker. Cooker runs win 38-46%, below blender, microwave and fizz, and its damage share is 2.8-3.5%.

Checked the shop UI with a screenshot (scratchpad/balance/pips3.png): 6 pips fit, and the tier rows show 2/4/6. All set texts read SET_THRESHOLDS dynamically. I also updated docs/item-hooks-refactor.md.
open: Late Shift dropped from 16.2% to 4.2% (seed 1). The spec only asked about Evening. Late may need its own softening.
The aisle 7 death rate among runs that reach it is 33%, close to the old 35% ceiling.

The Frying Pan is the dominant base weapon: 41-45% as a starting weapon, against 25% for the Toaster and 15-18% for the Nail Gun. The gap predates the ★3 behaviors and holds in runs without a ★3 Pan (36-39%). Base weapon numbers are not in this unit's knob list.
Runs that end with a ★3 Nail Gun win only about 17%, the same as without it. Its ★3 (spread burst) seems worth nothing in the proxy.
The Checkout interest caps (6/10) are still unmeasured as a separate knob under 2/4/6. Checkout L2 at run end is 18.8%, L3 4.3%.
The bowlingball (11.6%) and moldybread (10.4%) goals sit near the 10% floor. Only a few builds trigger Shatter or Detonate, so a lower need moves the share little.

With the 38 s aisles, aisle 1 leaves 8.8 of 30 groceries unkilled on average, and shop-1 coins fell by 2.6. A human playtest should judge whether aisle 1 feels too hectic for new players. The lab simulates no aisle events, so EVENT_LEAD is covered only by a unit test.
Every number is a build-lab proxy number. A human playtest is still needed to calibrate them, as docs/buildlab.md states.

nonBlocking: src/data/unlocks.ts:107 with src/state/profile.ts:118-123: goalBest is persisted. Changing goldstar's measure from maxTier to maxTier-1 breaks old saves. A stored best of 2 (a player who only ever had a ★2 item) now meets target 2, which means ★3, so goldstar unlocks without a ★3 item. A stored 1 shows 1/2 instead of 0/2. Fixing it would need a profile migration or a new goal key, and the spec suggested this design, so I did not block on it.
Binder, pricegun, snowcone and the other loosened needs only get easier against old stored goalBest values, so they cause no wrong unlocks.

src/engine/patterns/pulse.ts:42 reads w.tune.blowback with no '?? 0', while the other ★3 patterns (aura, puddle, cone) default their tune. This is harmless today because the Vacuum is the only pulse weapon.

The spec asked to measure the per-set L2 and L3 shares. docs/buildlab.md reports only Kitchen and Tools L3 (18.5% and 22.2%) and the commit message for the 2/4/6 change gives the same two figures. I did not rerun the batch, so I could not check the other sets' shares.
Aisles 1 and 2 keep their old enemy counts and only get shorter (38 s). Enemies per second rise by about 58%, which fits the spec's intent, but the spec literally says 'spawn counts adjusted'.
The Vacuum ★3 is a blowback knockback rather than the spec's example slow. The spec allows any one behavior, and the pushes(2)/pushes(3)/pushes(4) test covers it.
